rulings.ruling: The ten goals stay on both lanes. Performance is measured as Sam's five priorities P1 to P5 on the fixed writer trace, with provisional bars that calibration may tighten and only Sam may loosen; the 20 golden scenarios are part of done; Sam's must-haves are requirements per engine (native or documented workaround with its own passing tests), never knockout gates; year-one size (10m entities, 100m active facts, retained history) is the measurement size, not a target in itself.

rulings.topic: no silent precision loss (Sam's corrected numeric rule)
rulings.ruling: Exact storage and round trip for every value kind in use; order-preserving comparison for any attribute used in a range rule; a hard error, never silent conversion, for any value the engine cannot hold; integer range of at least 2^53; arithmetic over many rows only where a projection needs it. Arithmetic runs in the TypeScript kernel per subject; money is a scaled integer or an order-preserving decimal string; never floats for business values. The full signed 64-bit range is not required.

Not required for done. Required: (a) repository and every supported native fragment exact over the value domain each lane accepts; (b) the raw dataset exact on its documented exact channels; (c) raw natively typed shapes outside exact ranges are per-cell KNOWN-LIMIT exceptions, each with an exact mapped recipe, the obligation that qualifies it, and the original raw failure kept as a diagnostic with its unchanged expected answer. QLever integers beyond +/-2^59 are rejected at write instead of being an exception. Supported fragments have a fixed minimum coverage set.
Superseded by RESCOPE: performance is measured as NS.P1 to NS.P5 and the GS scenarios.
Kept as a declared step that reads no data, counted inside the task's measured call.
Superseded by RESCOPE.
A fresh agent given only the raw-query guide and the engine's public docs authors the raw query set; answers must match the repository at the same basis.
Assertion-level provenance: every answer row that claims a fact names its supporting assertion ids and transactions.
Not required for done. The packaged SDK consumer is required.

Where a projection needs an engine-side sum: exact total; typed integer-overflow only when the final result is outside the integer range; intermediate partial sums never wrap. Per-subject sums run in the kernel.
Typed preflight error unless the query converts explicitly; with explicit conversion to binary64, binary64 of the exact sum divided by the count, rounded once.
Typed error; no NaN or Infinity results.
Follow core comparison semantics; where core is silent, different type families are not equal and do not share a group.
Not a conflict: one value, several supports (PLAN C5.1).
Set semantics, duplicates collapsed, canonical value order (codepoint for text, numeric for numbers, then type family).
Policy draft EXP-P01, provisional orchestrator ruling, flagged to Sam; the three G9 obligations stay policy-pending until then.

The verifier covers every claimed obligation; at the year-one population and under the north-star workload it independently re-evaluates retained answer bytes, fault outcomes and coverage for every ladder level, scenario and rung, plus at least one spot rerun per profile unit.
Superseded by RESCOPE; its principle survives: read priorities P1, P4 and P5 are measured separately per surface (XTQL, SQL, SPARQL).
Aligned with PLAN C5: repository and fragments fail with ConflictingValuesError; the raw convenience shape is documented as non-equivalent; the canonical conflict-aware relation is values(attribute).

Where a projection needs an engine-side sum on XTDB, the primary recipe is the split-sum (32-bit halves recombined with overflow-checked arithmetic, verified in R12); SUM(CAST(x AS DECIMAL(38,0))) only if proven exact on 2.2.0 (KL-X7).
boolean < integer < number < datetime < string < ref < json < blob, then by value inside a family.

One value for identity, grouping and set membership (core CanonicalJson normalizes -0); when supports differ only in representation, the returned representation is the one from the support with the lowest recorded position; single-assertion reads return the stored representation.
Correctly rounded exact total on repository and supported-fragment surfaces where offered; a differing native SUM is a raw KNOWN-LIMIT with a mapped recipe.
Typed preflight error.

languageRules.substep: Every read substep records exactly one language: xtql (native.select), sql (selectSql), sparql (QLever native). A lane receipt counts a task only when every relational substep is in the lane's language.
languageRules.hybrid: A task with a relational substep in another language, or with a host step not listed below, counts for neither XTDB language.

permittedHostSteps.rule: A declared normalization step that reads no data: arithmetic or classification over values already returned by native substeps of the same task (for example BigInt subtraction of two returned sums). It is declared in the frozen task recipe, recorded in the trace, and its time is counted inside the task's measured call.
C8 frontier control for recursive reads, limited to the operations in FRONTIER_RULES. All relational evaluation stays native at one fixed cut.

frontierRules.source: PLAN v1.1 C8; acceptance review r1 finding 16
permittedHostOperations: subtract the visited set from the new frontier
test termination (empty frontier, maxRounds reached, maxRecursiveRows reached)
bind the next frontier as query parameters, chunked so each native query stays within its declared parameter bound
count rows and rounds against the bounds
forbiddenHostOperations: filtering on values, types, entity types or time
negation, aggregation, ordering or pagination of answers
any read that does not go through the lane's native language
frontierRules.fixedCut: Every round runs at the same captured basis (scope, P, optional R, V); each round's trace records that basis and the evaluator checks they are identical.
frontierRules.bounds: maxRounds and maxRecursiveRows are declared per task. Reaching a bound fails with the typed recursion-limit error (ERROR_TABLE E-RECURSION-LIMIT) and returns no partial answer.
frontierRules.cost: Host frontier time and peak host memory are counted inside the task's measured cost and reported per round.
frontierRules.noMutation: No round writes engine state (engine-side mutation count unchanged across the read).
frontierRules.accounting: A task whose host steps are only HS-FRONTIER (and HS-NORMALIZE) operations counts as pure in the lane's language.

valueKinds.rule: exact codepoint sequence; ill-formed UTF-16 rejected with E-INVALID-VALUE

exact; every lane accepts at least [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]; each lane declares its accepted range (LANE_INTEGER_RANGE); a value outside the lane's range fails the write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE and leaves no residue; never wrapped, widened or rounded
binary64 for approximate, deterministic values only (for example a risk score), never business values; stored and read bit-exact; NaN and infinities rejected

NEW value kind for money and business decimals: a scaled integer (declared scale) or an order-preserving decimal string; exact storage and round trip; order-preserving encoding for range rules; a value with more fractional digits than the declared scale or outside the declared magnitude fails with E-DECIMAL-UNREPRESENTABLE, never rounded; arithmetic in the TypeScript kernel (exact decimal or BigInt)
exact epoch-millisecond instant including fractional milliseconds; values needing nanoseconds use ISO strings (NUMERIC table)
exact text with key order kept; canonical form for identity

xtdb.rule: values inside are stored exactly; the lane may accept the whole core integer range

qlever.rule: values outside are rejected at write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any engine mutation (TARGETS section 3)

rangeRule: Every attribute used in a range rule (for example 'pay rate at or above 16.50', 'hours over 40') has an order-preserving comparison on every surface that serves the rule: native exact types inside their exact range, or a documented order-preserving channel.

numericOps.op: integer + integer, integer - integer, integer * integer (kernel; any surface that offers it)
numericOps.rule: exact; a result outside the core integer type range [-2^63, 2^63-1] fails with E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW; a result the target lane cannot store fails at write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE
quotient truncated toward zero; divisor 0 fails with E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO; -2^63 / -1 fails with E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW
a - trunc(a/b)*b (sign of the dividend); divisor 0 fails with E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO
exact; -(-2^63) and ABS(-2^63) fail with E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW
preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless the query converts one operand explicitly
numericOps.source: compiler.ts:556-560 ('Mixed exact integer and number arithmetic requires an explicit cast')

numericOps.rule: IEEE 754 binary64, round to nearest, ties to even, one rounding per operation; a finite result is returned bit-exact; an infinite result fails with E-NUMBER-OVERFLOW; divisor zero (+0.0 or -0.0) fails with E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO; NaN is never produced or stored

conversionRules.rule: toNumber(integer): round to nearest binary64, ties to even, once
toInteger(number): only explicit; the value must be integral and inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION; -0.0 converts to 0
CAST text to integer: canonical decimal only (optional leading '-', no '+', no leading zeros except '0', no '-0'), inside integer, else E-INVALID-CONVERSION or E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW
no implicit conversion between families anywhere (filters, joins, group keys, aggregates)

comparisonRules.rule: same family: exact comparison (integer as integers, binary64 by IEEE value, text by Unicode codepoint sequence, datetime by instant, boolean false < true, ref by id codepoints)
an untyped numeric constant compares by numeric value with number and datetime values (number 7 and datetime 7 both equal 7); text '7' is not equal
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog equality predicates compare numeric values as numbers' (packages/testkit/src/index.ts:721)

comparisonRules.rule: integer versus number: equality is false and they never share a group; an ordered comparison across them is preflight E-MIXED-FAMILY unless converted explicitly
comparisonRules.source: RULINGS Q8d (core silent for stored integer versus number)

comparisonRules.rule: entity ids and ref identities compare only with text or ref constants; a numeric or boolean constant is never equal and != is true
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog equality keeps identity bindings string-typed'

comparisonRules.rule: an untyped string constant matches string and ref values; a typed ref constant matches only ref values
comparisonRules.source: testkit 'datalog untyped strings match string and ref values while typed refs stay exact'

comparisonRules.rule: boolean true and integer 1 are distinct values and distinct groups
comparisonRules.source: packet oracle identity() (event_oracles.py: bool true vs i64 one)

comparisonRules.rule: -0.0 and +0.0 are one value for identity, grouping and set membership; when supports differ only in representation, the returned representation is the one from the support with the lowest recorded position; a single-assertion read returns the stored representation

aggregateRules.rule: SUM over integers, where a surface or projection offers it: exact total over the solution rows (bag of distinct bindings); E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW only when the final total is outside the integer range; partial sums never wrap. Engine-side sums are required only for projections that declare them (G5.agg.projection-sums); per-subject sums run in the kernel
aggregateRules.source: RULINGS Q8a, NUMERIC; compiler.ts SUM over DECIMAL(32,0)

aggregateRules.rule: SUM over number, where offered: the correctly rounded value of the exact sum (one rounding), independent of evaluation order
AVG over integers without explicit conversion: preflight E-INTEGER-AVG
AVG(toNumber(integer)) and AVG(number): binary64 of the exact sum divided by the count, rounded once
COUNT over a variable counts distinct flattened values of that variable (core), so two entities with value 10 count 1 while SUM counts 20
aggregateRules.source: testkit 'datalog aggregates preserve duplicate rows and define empty and distinct results'

aggregateRules.rule: ungrouped aggregate over no rows returns one row: COUNT 0; SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX null
grouped aggregate over no rows returns no rows; an empty group never appears
aggregateRules.source: wiki/problems/native-correlation.md (grouped empty SUM produces no row)

aggregateRules.rule: MIN/MAX return the extreme value; a witness query keeps every tied entity
packet tasks that state COALESCE(sum, 0) return 0 for an empty input; this is task-specific and recorded in the task recipe

cardManyOrder.rule: set semantics: equal values collapse to one element; elements ordered first by type family, then by value

valueOrder.decimal: exact numeric value (1.50 and 1.5 are one value)
valueOrder.ref: codepoint sequence of the target id
valueOrder.json: codepoint sequence of the canonical JSON text
valueOrder.blob: codepoint sequence of the content id

cardManyOrder.note: Family order per RULINGS Q14a; decimal sorts with integer and number by numeric value only inside its own family (decimal is ordered after number).

constraintRules.rule: with enforcement on, a command is rejected only when its post-state creates a new violation or worsens an existing one at some represented valid-time boundary; a pre-existing violation does not block an unrelated command and stays readable
write-time cardinality counts live assertions, including equal-valued duplicates (unchanged)
a card-one conflict that predates the enforcing write stays a conflict (C5.2) and reads per C5.3

commitOutcomes.source: PLAN v1.1 C2 (QLever), XTDB adapter commit path (lab/research/R4 3.2, 3.7); acceptance review r1 finding 5
commitOutcomes.witnessRule: The expected outcome after a fault is chosen from the last transition with durable or engine-side evidence observed by the fault injector after the crash (the log file's records read back, the engine's committed transactions, the publication marker), never from the system's own claim. A transition the protocol declares but the receipt does not witness fails the case.

outcomes.reads: E-REPAIRING while fenced; after recovery all access paths agree

cursorTransitions.source: acceptance review r1 finding 15; response r1 decision 12 (old cursors and bases route to the exact ledger path)

An available retained cut never becomes unavailable because its projection, mapping or index changed.

entrypoints.EP-FEED: The ordered, resumable change feed: entries carry tx, entity, attribute and the valid-time range affected; consumers resume from a checkpoint.

entrypoints.EP-EXPLAIN: Public plan and route capture for repository queries and native reads.
entrypoints.EP-PKG: Packed tarballs installed in a clean consumer outside the workspace; only public exports imported.
entrypoints.EP-ENGINE-ADMIN: Engine administrative and update routes (QLever update endpoint with and without the broker token, rebuild-index, checkpoint), used only to test refusal (C3).

selectorSemantics: An obligation's cases are a list of {set, select}. select is a list of tags or named required case ids; 'all' selects every case of the set. The evaluator resolves the selection against the set's pinned manifest (lab/acceptance/cases/<set>.json, sha256 pinned in the contract version): the selected cases are those carrying any listed tag, plus any named case listed by id. The resolution must be non-empty, every listed entry must be in the set's requiredTags or requiredCases, and every requiredCases id must exist in the manifest. A set whose manifest is not pinned in the contract version cannot close any obligation. Declared executions = selected cases x modes (x 1 per receipt scope key).

verifierModes.rerun: The verifier reruns the obligation's full selection on the same profile and recomputes every verdict from retained objects.
verifierModes.re-evaluate-and-spot: The verifier independently re-evaluates every retained answer byte, fault outcome and coverage record for every ladder level, scenario, rung and run, and performs at least one spot rerun per profile unit (one per lane and NS measurement; one per lane and golden scenario; one per lane and rung).

applicability.source: lab/PLAN.md section 1 item 7; acceptance review r1 finding 12
boundIdentities: acceptance-rule version (contract transitive hash and obligation definition hash)
applicability.carryForward: A receipt carries forward to a later profile only when every bound identity is unchanged, checked by an explicit applicability record (AP) that recomputes each identity on the later profile. Carry-forward serves intermediate tracking only.
applicability.finalAcceptance: The final acceptance of the selected integrated profile is entirely fresh: every obligation, including scale rungs and load levels, runs on that profile; nothing carries into it.

statusAlgorithm: for each lane L and integrated profile T:
for each obligation O with L in O.lanes:
key = L if O.receiptScope == 'lane' else engineOfLane[L]
A = acceptance receipts for (O.id, key) on T that pass VA (using VC records they cite)
closed(O, L, T) = O.grounding != 'policy-pending' and every case set of O is pinned
and A non-empty and every rule in O.closure.rules holds by its recompute
and VV-valid verifier coverage exists per VERIFIER_MODES[verifierMode(O)]
closed(section, L, T) = all closed(O, L, T) for O with section in O.goals
done(T) = closed for every section and lane, with every receipt fresh on T (APPLICABILITY.finalAcceptance)

OBS-CANCEL.verdict: PASS iff callerError matches E-CANCELLED or E-TIMEOUT as the case pins, transportAck observed, the request id absent from every engine sample after tDrained with tDrained - tCancelRequested <= T-DRAIN-MS, sample gaps <= 1000 ms over [tCancelRequested, tDrained + 5000 ms], and the reuse query on the same connection succeeds

OBS-PREABORT.verdict: PASS iff zero engine statements carry the request id over the full coverage window

OBS-CONNECTIONS.verdict: PASS iff every sample <= declared max and the count equals baseline within T-CONN-RELEASE-MS after tClose

OBS-SCRATCH.verdict: PASS iff countAfter = countBefore for every scratch relation and every unknown working outcome is resolved

OBS-NO-MUTATION.verdict: PASS iff the engine's committed-transaction or update counter is unchanged across the read

OBS-RESOURCE.verdict: PASS iff every peak <= forecast <= envelope (and <= T-PLANNER-MEM-BYTES where named)

OBS-AVAILABILITY.verdict: PASS iff a write and a read both succeed at some t <= tFailure + T-AVAIL-WINDOW-MS with no manual restart event

OBS-SCALE-COUNT.verdict: PASS iff the count query's answer equals O-REPLAY's analytic count

OBS-WORK.verdict: ratio of work units between the compared operations, evaluated against the named witness threshold

OBS-MAINTENANCE.verdict: events present; lag statistics against the named threshold

OBS-FAULT-TRANSITIONS.verdict: the last witnessed transition is the last one whose durable evidence is present after the crash

specRules: Positive witnesses assert exact types with an Equals<A, B> helper; assignability alone does not count.
Every asserted type is also checked not to be any (IsAny<T> is false); an accidental any fails.

Negative witnesses do not use @ts-expect-error; tsc runs on the witness set and the observed set of {file, line, column, code} must equal the pinned expected set exactly (CMP-DIAGNOSTICS); an unrelated diagnostic fails.
The emitted public declarations are scanned: no exported symbol resolves to any except an explicitly listed allowlist in the witness manifest.
Witnesses import only from packed public package exports, compiled with the consumer's strict tsconfig.

obligations.title: Unchanged44 on the lane foundation
obligations.statement: The unchanged 44-case shared conformance suite (CS-U44) passes against the lane engine's Triples foundation in current and reopened form: 44 named cases per mode, zero skipped.

obligations.title: Every value kind in use round-trips exactly on every surface
obligations.statement: Every case of CS-TYPES8 (one assertion per value kind of VALUE_KINDS with the listed edge values, integers inside the lane's declared range) reads back exactly through Triples, the repository, the lane's native surface with a schema-derived contract, and the documented raw recipe, in current, reopen and engine-restart modes.

obligations.title: Values a lane cannot hold fail with a typed error, never silently
obligations.statement: Every lane accepts every integer in [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1]; every CS-RANGE-OUT case (integers beyond the lane's declared LANE_INTEGER_RANGE, for QLever beyond +/-2^59) fails the write with E-VALUE-OUT-OF-RANGE before any engine mutation, with no residue on any access path, and is never wrapped, widened or rounded.

obligations.title: Decimal value kind for money and business decimals
obligations.statement: Every CS-DECIMAL case: decimals are stored as a scaled integer or an order-preserving decimal string and round-trip exactly on every surface; range rules (for example 'pay rate at or above 16.50') compare in exact numeric order on the repository, fragments and documented raw channel; a value beyond the declared scale or magnitude fails with E-DECIMAL-UNREPRESENTABLE, never rounded; kernel arithmetic over decimals is exact.
sources: lab/TARGETS.md section 3 (decimal value kind on the critical path for goal 1)

obligations.title: Invalid values are rejected atomically
obligations.statement: Every case of CS-TYPES8-NEG is rejected with its pinned error (E-INVALID-VALUE or E-UNSUPPORTED-VALUE); the committed position is unchanged, no receipt or claim exists, and no partial row or triple is visible through any access path.

obligations.title: Later writes never change an earlier exact read
obligations.statement: After the heterogeneous writes of CS-WIDEN, every earlier value still reads back bit-exact on every surface, current and reopen; documented raw columns stay monomorphic.

obligations.title: Native parameters keep exact values
obligations.statement: Parameters of every value family bound into a native query in the lane language (including -0.0, the edges of the lane's integer range, decimals, text with quote, $$ and ;) reach the engine with their exact value and type, current and reopen.

obligations.title: Required is enforced on new or worsened violations
obligations.statement: With enforcement on, a command whose post-state creates a new or worsened Required violation at a represented valid-time boundary fails with E-CONSTRAINT (reason required) and no residue; a pre-existing violation does not block an unrelated command and stays readable (CN-NEW-OR-WORSENED).

obligations.title: Cardinality is enforced with the specified counting rule
obligations.statement: With enforcement on, a new or worsened cardinality-one violation fails with E-CONSTRAINT (reason cardinality), counting live assertions including equal-valued duplicates (CN-CARD-COUNT); cardinality-many keeps every live value.

obligations.title: Uniqueness holds under concurrent writers
obligations.statement: A unique attribute value is live on at most one entity at any valid instant; a new violation fails with E-CONSTRAINT (reason unique); in a 16-way race for one value exactly one command commits.

obligations.title: Reference targets are enforced at represented boundaries
obligations.statement: With ReferenceTarget rules supplied, a new or worsened dangling reference fails with E-CONSTRAINT (reason reference-target); same-batch forward references are admitted.

obligations.title: Contracts derive from the active schema release
obligations.statement: Repository model types and native helper contracts derive from the active ConfigStore release; after a v1 -> v2 release the derived contracts change accordingly; every read reports the schema snapshot it used.

obligations.title: Native packet: 142 named executions in the lane language
obligations.statement: All 71 packet tasks run current and reopened (142 named executions) on the lane's native surface; every relational substep is in the lane's language; host steps are only HS-NORMALIZE and HS-FRONTIER; answers equal expected_rows and O-EVT.

obligations.title: Integer arithmetic is exact in the kernel and wherever offered
obligations.statement: Every CS-NUMERIC integer-scalar, conversion and range-rules case returns the NUMERIC_OPS or CONVERSION_RULES answer in the TypeScript kernel, including E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW, E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO and E-INVALID-CONVERSION; any repository or fragment surface that offers the operation returns the same answer or a typed error; no result is ever wrapped.

obligations.title: binary64 arithmetic follows IEEE and the frozen sign rules
obligations.statement: On the repository and supported native fragments, every CS-NUMERIC binary64 case returns the N-F-ARITH and N-F-NEGZERO answer bit-exact; division by zero fails with E-DIVISION-BY-ZERO and overflow with E-NUMBER-OVERFLOW.

obligations.title: Comparisons follow the frozen comparison table
obligations.statement: Every CS-NUMERIC cross-family case returns the COMPARISON_RULES answer (CMP-NUMERIC-CONST, CMP-INT-FLOAT, CMP-IDENTITY, CMP-UNTYPED-STRING, CMP-BOOL-INT, CMP-NEGZERO), including E-MIXED-FAMILY where stated, on the repository and supported native fragments.

obligations.title: Errors surface exactly as pinned
obligations.statement: Every CS-ERRORS case yields its pinned ERROR_TABLE error under ERROR_COMPARISON, never a success with partial rows.

obligations.title: Codepoint string order on the supported surfaces
obligations.statement: Repository queries and supported native fragments order, range-filter and page text in codepoint order: the frozen O-STR arrays and the O-COLL control pass unchanged, current and reopen.

obligations.title: Plans and routes are captured for every query
obligations.statement: Every repository query and native read in CS-QMIX returns its engine plan and Triplex route through EP-EXPLAIN, and O-PLAN's route verdict (OBS-PLAN-ROUTE) equals the C1 expected route.

obligations.title: Key-bounded access at 10m
obligations.statement: At P-YEAR-ONE the point, getMany, selective-filter and reverse-ref classes resolve through a key-bounded access path (OBS-PLAN-ACCESS), and their p50 ratio between P-RUNG-1M and P-YEAR-ONE stays within T-LAT-RATIO-10M-1M.

obligations.title: Expensive queries are refused before construction
obligations.statement: Every CS-ADMIT case fails with E-ADMISSION before the engine builds the expensive structure: zero scratch rows or graphs, engine memory within T-PLANNER-MEM-BYTES (OBS-RESOURCE), and the engine stays available.

obligations.title: Admitted queries stay inside their declared budget
obligations.statement: Every admitted CS-QMIX query at P-YEAR-ONE records estimate and actual cost (OBS-PLAN-COST); none exceeds its declared budget; a query crossing its budget stops with E-ADMISSION or E-TIMEOUT rather than running to completion.

obligations.title: Recursion is correct and bounded on every topology
obligations.statement: Recursive reads over every benchmark-contract topology (chain, tree, diamond, cycle, high-fanout, skewed-hotset) return O-REPLAY answers in the lane language and meet T-RECURSION-P99-MS at P-RUNG-1M and P-YEAR-ONE.

obligations.title: Recursive native reads never mutate and obey frontier rules
obligations.statement: Every C8-* case in CS-RECURSION-TOPO: engine-side mutation count is zero during the read (OBS-NO-MUTATION); all rounds run at one fixed cut; bounds fail with E-RECURSION-LIMIT and no partial answer; host steps are only FRONTIER_RULES operations; host time is counted.

obligations.title: Correlated negation on the supported surfaces
obligations.statement: The flat and nested correlated NOT EXISTS controls and their EXISTS, MINUS and OPTIONAL plus !BOUND variants return the O-SHAPE answers through the repository and supported native fragments.

obligations.title: Correlated negation on the XTDB raw surface
obligations.statement: The correlated NOT EXISTS controls written in raw SQL and raw XTQL over the documented raw dataset return only `two` (the QLever raw cell is exception RX-Q29, qualified by R.raw.mapped-recipes).

obligations.title: One cut per multi-call task under a concurrent writer
obligations.statement: Each multi-call task pins one captured basis for all its calls; a writer committed between calls does not change its answer; the next task sees the writer.

obligations.title: Conflict semantics per PLAN C5
obligations.statement: Every C5-* case of CS-CONFLICT: Equal-valued duplicates are not conflicts (one value, several supports); a conflict is two or more distinct live values of a cardinality-one attribute at the basis; get and getMany fail with E-CONFLICTING-VALUES listing every conflicted entity and attribute; find, counts, ordering, includes and negation fail with it when a referenced attribute is conflicted for any candidate, and are unaffected by unreferenced attributes; the values(attribute) relation lists every live value with its supports; the raw convenience shape returns its documented indicator and never certifies equivalence.

obligations.title: Aggregate edge shapes keep their specified answers
obligations.statement: AG-EMPTY-UNGROUPED, AG-EMPTY-GROUPED, AG-MINMAX-TIES and AG-PACKET-COALESCE cases of CS-SHAPE return the O-SHAPE answers on the repository and supported native fragments.

obligations.title: Aggregates follow the frozen support semantics
obligations.statement: Every CS-SUPPORT case returns the AG-SUM-I, AG-SUM-F and AG-COUNT answers (SUM over the bag of distinct solution rows, COUNT over distinct values) on the repository and supported native fragments.

obligations.title: Group keys keep typed identity
obligations.statement: Every CS-NUMERIC groups case groups by the COMPARISON_RULES identities on the repository and supported native fragments.
sources: testkit 'datalog having preserves typed group and aggregate equality'

obligations.title: Engine-side sums are exact where a projection needs them
obligations.statement: For every declared projection whose definition aggregates over many subjects, and every CS-NUMERIC projection-sums case, the engine-side SUM returns the AG-SUM-I total (exact; E-INTEGER-OVERFLOW only for a final total outside the integer range), using the split-sum recipe on XTDB (RULINGS Q13) or another qualified recipe; unconverted integer AVG fails with E-INTEGER-AVG; per-subject sums run in the kernel and are covered by G2.arith.integer-exact.
sources: lab/research/SAM-pasted-numbers-2026-11-07.md section 5 (arithmetic over many rows only where a projection needs it)

obligations.title: Cancellation observed down to drained engine work
obligations.statement: Cancelling a long read in the lane language yields an OBS-CANCEL verdict DRAINED: caller settled with E-CANCELLED, transport cancel acknowledged, engine stops listing the statement within T-DRAIN-MS, same connection reused healthily.

obligations.title: Deadlines are enforced end to end
obligations.statement: A read exceeding timeoutMs returns E-TIMEOUT within T-DEADLINE-GRACE-MS and drains per OBS-CANCEL within T-DRAIN-MS; a non-interruptible engine operation is prevented by admission or drained within the bound.

obligations.title: A pre-aborted request does no engine work
obligations.statement: A request cancelled before dispatch returns E-CANCELLED and OBS-PREABORT records zero engine statements for its request id.

obligations.title: No scratch residue after reads, cancels and crashes
obligations.statement: After normal operation, cancellation and crash plus documented recovery, every remaining scratch relation (constraint and Datalog scratch; native reads create none per C8) holds zero rows for finished work (OBS-SCRATCH) and every working-outcome-unknown is resolved.

obligations.title: Connections and engine work are bounded and released
obligations.statement: Engine-side connections never exceed the declared pool caps across 100 open-use-close cycles and under 1024 logical clients, and return to baseline within T-CONN-RELEASE-MS after close (OBS-CONNECTIONS).

obligations.title: A resource failure does not take the engine down
obligations.statement: A read exceeding the engine memory budget fails with E-ADMISSION or a pinned execution error; writes and reads succeed again within T-AVAIL-WINDOW-MS without manual restart (OBS-AVAILABILITY).

obligations.title: Commands are all-or-nothing on every access path
obligations.statement: Every CS-WRITE atomic case and every CS-FAULT atomic fault point leaves the complete command or nothing, as seen through every listed access path; a later successful write never publishes a partial earlier one.

obligations.title: A command id commits at most once
obligations.statement: A duplicate commandId, sequentially and in a 16-way race, commits exactly once; every other attempt gets E-COMMAND-COMMITTED with the original txId; transactionByCommand returns it.

obligations.title: Preconditions and concurrency never lose an update
obligations.statement: Stale TripleLive and EntityState preconditions fail with E-TX-CONFLICT; concurrent conflicting writers lose no acknowledged update; replay-safe retries reach the O-REPLAY final state.

obligations.title: Receipts are complete and ordered
obligations.statement: Every acknowledged command has a transaction record whose position, instant, actor, commandId, correlationId, causationId, configSnapshot and ordered changes equal O-REPLAY; reserved namespaces fail with E-RESERVED; every ACK has a durable operation receipt.

obligations.title: The logical journal stays queryable (C6)
obligations.statement: Every C6-* case: direct match and Datalog queries over :_tx/change and :_tx/changed-entity, transactions(), transactionsForEntity and transactionByCommand return O-REPLAY's outputs, order and -0 behavior; a physically slimmed journal synthesizes byte-identical results.

obligations.title: Commit outcomes follow the witnessed transition table
obligations.statement: For every C2-* (QLever) and X-* (XTDB) fault point of CS-FAULT, injected T-FAULT-REPS times, the final state, the original caller's outcome, retries with the same commandId and reads match COMMIT_OUTCOMES for the last witnessed transition: a group with QT2-LOGGED evidence is always published by recovery; retries before publication return E-COMMIT-PENDING or E-REPAIRING; a success receipt exists only after publication.

obligations.title: One mutator, credentials, epochs and fence (C3)
obligations.statement: Every C3-* case: an old broker resuming after replacement cannot mutate; updates without the broker token are refused by the engine; native reads and the raw hatch cannot route an update; rebuild, checkpoint and administration are refused while fenced; commits while fenced return E-REPAIRING; a new broker closes the previous epoch before mutating.

obligations.title: Backup and restore reproduce every read
obligations.statement: A stopped backup restored into a fresh engine reproduces every frozen cut on every surface and accepts new writes at the next position.

obligations.title: Schema evolution with live data and resumable backfill
obligations.statement: For each CS-MIGRATION case, with old and new clients concurrent: bases before the release read with the old mapping, after it the new; a backfill killed midway resumes to the O-REPLAY state; old cursors continue per CURSOR_TRANSITIONS (CT-RELEASE-CHANGE); history is preserved.

obligations.title: Valid Triplex writes are never rejected for the physical design
obligations.statement: Every CS-MIGRATION valid-writes case that O-REPLAY classifies as valid is accepted and read correctly on every surface.

obligations.title: Projection eligibility routes whole queries (C1)
obligations.statement: Every C1-* case of CS-ELIGIBILITY: the observed route (OBS-PLAN-ROUTE) equals the C1 expected route for the whole query, including a partial entity excluded by an early filter but relevant to ordering, negation or aggregation, a mapping-generation mismatch, explicit and decreasing recorded times, interior positions and V outside the marker window; answers equal O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: Every read sees one coherent publication
obligations.statement: Under concurrent commit groups every read's answer equals O-REPLAY at its returned basis; no read mixes two publications of ledger, projection, schema or index state.

obligations.title: Requested bases are honored and returned bases are true
obligations.statement: A read at a requested basis is answered at exactly that basis; the only permitted errors are those of CURSOR_TRANSITIONS.permittedErrors; the returned basis is the basis used; after an ACK at P the writing client's next latest read returns a basis at or after P.

obligations.title: Valid-time boundaries take effect without new writes
obligations.statement: When a validFrom or validTo boundary passes with no command, reads at valid instants beyond it reflect it on every surface, before and after maintenance.

obligations.title: Bounded boundary maintenance (C4)
obligations.statement: Every C4-* case of CS-MAINT: update operations stay within the bound; a large boundary enters MAINTAINING; writes to entities in pending chunks are projected at the target instant; crash and resume completes from durable progress; the qualified hatch returns E-MAINTAINING or exact results throughout MAINTAINING; repository reads route exact; two facts with the same expiry, one deleted, read correctly; delta backpressure engages.

obligations.title: Reuse is real, bounded, keyed and invalidated
obligations.statement: For each reuse mechanism the lane declares (at least the projection and one maintained closure or cache), CS-REUSE shows: a second read at the same key does at most T-REUSE-AVOIDED of the first read's engine work (OBS-WORK); answers equal a run with reuse disabled; an affecting write invalidates the entry for later bases; the cache stays within its declared cap.

obligations.title: Supports are maintained incrementally
obligations.statement: At P-RUNG-1M a one-entity change to a maintained support or projection costs at most T-INCR-WORK of full recomputation (OBS-WORK), and the maintained result equals a fresh recomputation and O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: Maintained supports survive partial retraction
obligations.statement: Removing one of two supports keeps a derived fact; removing the last removes it; for workload 20, CS-SUPPORT-DAG and identical assertions where one is retracted.

obligations.title: Half-open valid intervals on every surface
obligations.statement: Valid intervals are [validFrom, validTo) with null open-ended, exact at fractional-millisecond boundaries and at the boundary instants, on every surface, current, reopen and engine restart.

obligations.title: Recorded-time and position cuts are exact, independently
obligations.statement: Reads by recordedAt and by position equal O-REPLAY, with R evaluated independently of P: between commits, at an instant shared by two commits, with decreasing recorded instants from a second runtime, at interior positions of nested transactions, after corrections and around aborts; ordinary reads take R and V only.

obligations.title: Ordinary history keeps the raw lifetime contract
obligations.statement: Ordinary Triples.history, match, entity and entities keep the raw assertion-lifetime contract exactly as O-REPLAY computes it.

obligations.title: As-of snapshots hide retirements not yet known
obligations.statement: The five failing tiny-v4 checks, the finite-nine fixture and the same-R control pass through the repository timeline and as-of reads and the native history helpers: retirement fields are null until known at the cut and equal O-REPLAY after.

obligations.title: Corrections preserve what was previously recorded
obligations.statement: A correction keeps the earlier value visible at earlier recorded cuts and both versions in history, on every surface, current, reopen and restart.
sources: testkit 'historical corrections preserve what was previously recorded'

obligations.title: Answer rows name their supporting assertions
obligations.statement: Every repository and native helper answer row that claims a fact names its supporting assertion ids and transactions, equal to O-REPLAY's supports.

obligations.title: Presence follows the frozen policy
obligations.statement: Presence toggles preserve domain facts and reference targets; configured-entity membership at a cut follows the frozen presence policy on every surface.

obligations.title: Entity deletion keeps its contract and history
obligations.statement: The existing delete contract holds and interval-local deletion follows the frozen deletion policy with preserved history.

obligations.title: Restrict, detach and bounded cascade
obligations.statement: Restrict, detach and bounded reverse cascade follow the frozen cascade policy with deterministic receipts and atomic refusal over budget.

obligations.title: Packaged SDK consumer slice
obligations.statement: From packed tarballs in a clean consumer outside the workspace, an application uses the repository, the writer and native queries: a write, a repository read, an authored native read in the lane language, history, a receipt, a cursor continuation and a reopen all equal O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: Public types derive from the schema
obligations.statement: Against the packed declarations, the CS-TYPEWITNESS witnesses meet ACCEPTANCE 6.5: exact type assertions hold, no accidental any, and the expected diagnostics occur at their pinned codes and locations only.

obligations.title: Production scope ownership is enforced (C7.1, C7.2)
obligations.statement: C7-OWNER-MISMATCH, C7-OWNER-RECORD-INIT, C7-DOMAIN-ONLY-CURRENT, C7-NO-STAGING-DOMAIN and C7-XTDB-TABLE-NAMES: a mismatched scope fails with E-SCOPE-OWNER before touching projection storage; domain-pattern raw queries see only current domain data.

obligations.title: Shared-engine scopes never leak (C7.3)
obligations.statement: C7-SHARED-COLLISION: two scopes with identical entity ids on one engine; the repository, helpers and scope-selecting raw recipes return only their own scope's data.

obligations.title: Cursors are complete and snapshot-stable
obligations.statement: CS-CURSOR stable cases: pages are deterministic, traverse the complete snapshot with no duplicate or skipped row under concurrent writes, and a cursor issued at P1 continues at P1 after the publication advances.

obligations.title: Deep pages stay cheap at 10m
obligations.statement: At P-YEAR-ONE page 10,000 costs at most T-DEEP-PAGE-RATIO of page 1.

obligations.title: Cursors and historical bases continue across transitions
obligations.statement: Every CURSOR_TRANSITIONS.mustContinue case continues with O-REPLAY's rows at the cursor's basis; errors occur only in the permittedErrors cases, each with its pinned error; CE-FENCED also continues after recovery.

obligations.title: Advertised capabilities are true and cover the fixed set
obligations.statement: The advertised fragment capability set includes every FRAGMENT_COVERAGE row; each advertised capability has a passing case; each unadvertised one fails with a pinned error.

obligations.title: Open, close and reopen are clean
obligations.statement: initialize is idempotent across restarts; close releases every connection and background task (OBS-CONNECTIONS); reopen after close works.

obligations.title: Native entry checks in the lane language
obligations.statement: The native entry checks of CS-ENTRY pass fresh, current and reopen, every read check in the lane's language.

obligations.title: Native reads cannot write and parameters cannot inject
obligations.statement: Native read surfaces refuse every write form with E-READ-ONLY and no engine mutation (OBS-NO-MUTATION); bound parameters with quote, $$, ; and newlines are data.

obligations.title: Entity suite against the independent oracle
obligations.statement: Every case of CS-ENTITY passes through the repository and writer, current, reopen and engine restart; expected answers only from O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: The suites kill every mutant
obligations.statement: Every mutation control meets MUTANT_RULE against its targeted cases on the lane.

obligations.title: Raw queries return what the entity API returns
obligations.statement: For every RP-* class of CS-RAW-RECIPES, a raw query written only from the raw-query guide returns the repository's answer at the same basis and O-REPLAY's, in the lane language, through the raw hatch and direct wire access, over every value outside the lane's RAW_EXCEPTIONS domains.

obligations.title: Every raw exception's mapped recipe is exact; originals kept as diagnostics
obligations.statement: For each RAW_EXCEPTIONS cell of the lane, its RXC-* case runs the mapped recipe over the full exempt domain and returns O-REPLAY's answer; every named DIAGNOSTICS entry runs in the same receipt with its unchanged expected answer and retained actual answer.

obligations.title: Raw recipes are authored from the guide alone

obligations.title: P1: many concurrent pinned reads that never block writers (per surface)
obligations.statement: With the fixed writer trace running, closed-loop readers at 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256 (and 1,024 stress) each name their basis (valid time and record time or tx), in the lane's language; per level the receipt records correctness-qualified read goodput and p99 and writer commit latency and throughput; every NS-P1-* bar holds: zero violations, goodput at 256 not below 64, read p99 within NS-P1-READ-P99-256-MS, writer commit p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-256 of its zero-reader baseline, no command waits beyond NS-P1-WRITER-WAIT-MAX-MS, and at 1,024 goodput within NS-P1-GOODPUT-1024-VS-256, writer p99 within NS-P1-WRITER-P99-RATIO-1024, back to the 256-level bar within NS-P1-RECOVERY-MS.

obligations.title: P2: small, atomic, idempotent per-subject commits with low latency

obligations.title: P3: an ordered, resumable change feed

obligations.title: P4: a fast path to current values, separate from history (per surface)

obligations.title: The year-one measurement population exists and is counted
obligations.statement: At P-YEAR-ONE one deployment holds the SCALE_POPULATION year-one population (10m entities, 100m active domain facts, at least 150M retained facts, tenants and strata as specified) written through public writes; every stratum and separate count matches independent count queries (OBS-SCALE-COUNT) and O-REPLAY analytic counts. This is the size the priorities are measured at, not a target in itself.

obligations.title: Each rung passes before the next opens
obligations.statement: Rungs 10k, 100k, 1m and 10m subjects are admitted in order; each passes S.correctness.query-families at its own rung before the next is admitted.

obligations.title: Query families correct at every rung
obligations.statement: At every rung of P-RUNGS the query families (point, selective filter, join, anti-join, recursion, aggregate, historical, interval, pagination, subject pull) run on at least T-SAMPLES-PER-FAMILY samples with at least T-SAMPLES-PER-STRATUM in every applicable stratum plus complete-count queries, on the repository and in the lane language, all equal to O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: Runs fit the admitted envelope
obligations.statement: Every rung is admitted with a peak forecast (rebuild overlap, delta growth, pre-GC growth, WAL, log, checkpoints, backups, replay, host clients); observed peaks stay within it (OBS-RESOURCE); an over-budget rung is BLOCKED_CAPACITY and stays open.

obligations.title: Size and cost metrics are measured and reported separately
obligations.statement: At every rung: bytes per entity and fact, write amplification per component (BUDGET_COMPONENTS), history separately, ingest rate, rebuild or compaction time, restart time, peak RSS per owner, peak disk.

obligations.title: Maintenance at year one keeps reads correct
obligations.statement: Compaction, index rebuild and projection maintenance at P-YEAR-ONE complete; reads during and after equal O-REPLAY.

obligations.title: Restart at year one
obligations.statement: An engine restart at P-YEAR-ONE becomes available within the recorded time and every sampled old cut re-reads identically.

obligations.title: The integrated candidate stays inside frozen budgets
obligations.statement: At every rung the integrated candidate's complete-path cost (BUDGET_COMPONENTS, including log, broker and verification) and its NS measurements stay inside budgets.json, which is frozen before candidates, compared cumulatively against the frozen A0 control at the same rung.
